title: Apolisi m'boma la Mangochi amanga Davie Chunga, wazaka 31
excerpt: Apolisi m'boma la Mangochi amanga Davie Chunga, wazaka 31, yemwe ndi mphunzitsi pa Sukuku ya Pulayimale ya Mpondasi, pa mlandu woganiziridwa kuti anadya tangale wosatsuluza ndi mmodzi mwa ophunzira ake, mtsikana wa zaka 14 yemwe ndiwa sitandade 7. Mneneri wa Polisi ku Mangochi, Inspector Amina Tepani Daudi, wati kusaweruzikaku kunachitika pa 26 Julayi 2026. Malinga ndi Daudi, Chunga anakumana ndi mtsikanayo pamene amachokera kutchalitchi ndipo anamuyitana kunyumba kwake pomunyengerera kuti akamupatse maphunziro owonjezera. Atafika kunyumbako, akuti mphunzitsiyo anamukakamiza mtsikanayo kudya monyang'ama ndipo pambuyo pake anamupatsa ndalama zokwana K10,000. Mtsikanayo atabwerera kwawo, makolo ake atamufunsa komwe anali, adafotokoza zomwe zinamuchitikira. Nkhaniyi idakanenedwa ku polisi, pomwe mtsikanayo anatengedwa kuchipatala kuti akamuyezetse. Zotsatira za mayeso a kuchipatala zinasonyeza kuti mtsikanayo anachitidwadi monyang'ama. Chunga wamangidwa pa mlandu wogonana ndi mwana wamkazi, womwe uli motsutsana ndi Gawo 138 la Penal Code, ndipo akuyembekezeka kuonekera pamaso pa khoti kafukufuku wa polisi akamalizidwa. Pakadali pano, Polisi ku Mangochi yati kuyambira Januwale mpaka pano, yalandira milandu 35 yokhudza kugwiriridwa kwa ana aakazi, poyerekeza ndi milandu 21 yomwe adalandira nthawi yomweyi chaka chatha. (Wolemba: Esnath Kalawe-Lilongwe|28/07/26)

title: Bachelor's Degree holders eligible for secondary school recruitment
excerpt: The Ministry of Education has reaffirmed that only teachers with a Bachelor's Degree are eligible for this year's secondary school recruitment. Secretary for Education Dr. Ken Ndala said the government is following existing recruitment policies and cannot make exceptions for Diploma holders. He encouraged affected teachers to upgrade to Bachelor's Degree level to qualify for future recruitment. He also assured that teachers already employed in secondary schools with Diploma qualifications will retain their jobs and continue to be promoted under the current regulations.

title: Government to Train 5,000 Primary Teachers in New Methods
excerpt: Teamwork, effective school leadership, and recognising outstanding teachers could be the game changers in improving education standards in Mangochi District, according to Boma Zone Primary Education Advisor (PEA), Mariam Sambo. Speaking during TIWADZIWE, a weekly education programme organised by the Teachers of Mangochi platform, Sambo shared the leadership strategies that delivered consistent academic success during her tenure in Mkumba Zone, where she served for nearly 11 years. Under her leadership, Mkumba emerged as the district's top-performing education zone for four consecutive years before she was deployed in Boma Zone. She also unveiled new initiatives aimed at replicating and sustaining similar excellence in her current zone. She said quality education can not be achieved by teachers alone, stressing that meaningful progress depends on strong collaboration among school leaders, teachers, parents, and local communities.

she said. Sambo urged school administrators to strengthen instructional leadership by ensuring regular classroom supervision, completing the syllabus on time, providing remedial support to struggling learners, and encouraging the production and use of locally made teaching and learning materials. She also highlighted the impact of the Zonal Data Laboratory (ZDL) committees and the One-Hour Supervision Model, through which headteachers and deputy headteachers provide daily professional support to teachers through classroom observation. Widely recognised for championing teacher motivation, Sambo has made the recognition of excellence one of her signature initiatives. During the last school session in Boma Zone, she spearheaded an awards program that honored outstanding teachers for their dedication and performance. Learners who were selected to national secondary schools were also recognised with mattresses, writing materials, and cash prizes in recognition of their outstanding academic achievement. The initiative drew praise from education stakeholders for inspiring both teachers and learners to strive for excellence. Sambo announced that the awards program will return this year, revealing that several education partners have already pledged their support. She said a dedicated committee and transparent selection criteria will be established to ensure that deserving teachers and learners are fairly recognised.
she said. In her closing remarks, Sambo appealed to teachers, school leaders, parents, and learners to embrace unity and shared responsibility in transforming education.

title: Learners begin schools holiday
excerpt: As thousands of learners across Malawi begin their school holidays following the end-of-year examination results, education stakeholders are urging parents and guardians to offer support rather than criticism to children who did not perform as expected. The call comes in the wake of a tragic incident in Ntcheu District, where a 13-year-old Standard 7 learner from Chiole Primary School, Naomi Lazaro, reportedly died by suicide after failing examinations that would have qualified her for promotion to Standard 8. Information gathered indicates that the learner had allegedly been subjected to insults from some relatives over her examination results, a development that has left teachers, parents and members of the community mourning while raising concerns about the emotional impact of academic pressure on children. Education experts and child advocates have long maintained that examination results should not define a child's value or future. They argue that examinations assess performance at a particular point in time but do not determine intelligence, talent, character or a learner's potential to succeed in life. Teachers interviewed by this publication, who requested anonymity because they were not authorised to speak publicly on the matter, said schools should introduce counselling sessions immediately after the release of examination results to support learners struggling to cope with disappointment. They said many children need reassurance that poor academic performance is not the end of their educational journey and that encouragement from parents, teachers and guardians can help restore confidence and motivate them to work harder.

said one of the teachers. Education stakeholders are also encouraging families and communities to create supportive environments where children feel safe to discuss their emotions without fear of ridicule or rejection. As the debate on children's mental well-being continues, the Ntcheu tragedy serves as a reminder of the importance of responsible parenting, positive communication and emotional support during the examination period. Several attempts were made to contact Eye of the Child for comment on how learners who fail examinations should be supported. However, all phone calls went unanswered.
